A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, table, references, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A.6 report original FRL-versus-ERM experiments across five medical-image datasets, including IID and distribution-shift evaluations.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained in Section 5 and Appendix A.6, including subgroup accuracy results from the reported 660 training runs.

M1.justification: Both versions analyse the same fair-representation objective and evaluate the same marginal and class-conditional adversarial FRL methods. No algorithm, architecture, objective, or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both use CheXpert, MIMIC, HAM10000, Fitzpatrick17k, and PAPILA with eleven dataset–attribute combinations. The disease tasks, subgroup definitions, IID setting, and three injected-bias scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain ERM, marginal FRL from Kim et al. (2019), and conditional FRL. The conditional method's citation changes from Zhao et al. (2019) to Zhao et al. (2020), but identifies the same work and evaluated method.

E3.justification: Section 5, Appendix A.4–A.5, and Table 1 retain the same splitting and bias-generation procedures, accuracy-gap metric, architecture, training budget, hyperparameters, and stopping criteria. No additional experimental protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: The bias-mechanism comparisons, subgroup-separability analysis, and conditional-FRL repetitions are retained. The new causal diagrams in Appendix A.2 are conceptual examples, not additional robustness tests or empirical case studies.

E5.justification: Both report five random seeds, 660 training runs, Kendall's tau association tests, and the same standard-deviation error-bar practices. Neither repeated-run information nor uncertainty estimation changes.

E6.justification: All six performance plots retain their results: v1 Figures 2–7 correspond to v2 Figures 2–4 and 6–8. For example, Figure 4 retains tau = 0.600, p = 0.0099 for Group 0 and tau = 0.564, p = 0.0165 for Group 1.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a train/test indicator T, the mutual-information decomposition in Equation (9), and formal selection-mechanism examples. The central definitions, assumptions, lemmas, Proposition 4.8, and their proofs remain unchanged; the harmlessness definition receives equivalent explanatory wording.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and main conclusions retain the three fairness paradigms, IID futility claim, and hypotheses concerning causal bias structure and subgroup separability. The expanded appendix does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.2 adds discussion of causal versus anticausal settings, qualifies when counterfactual fairness implies demographic parity, and distinguishes subgroup disparities from train/test distribution shifts. It also discusses domain-generalisation connections while explicitly leaving broader claims outside the paper's scope.

D1.justification: Appendix A.4–A.5 and Table 1 retain the same preprocessing, subgroup construction, corruption implementation, hyperparameter-selection procedure, and training settings. No new implementation, hardware, or code/data-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: The extended discussion adds Federici et al. (2021), Rosenblatt and Witter (2022), and Silva (2024), connecting the work more explicitly to distribution-shift theory and counterfactual fairness. Other changed citation years and publication details concern retained works.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order are largely preserved. Appendix A.2 becomes an extended discussion with additional subheadings, and A.3 adds an explanation of the strict effectiveness inequality. There are also limited wording, affiliation, acknowledgement, and bibliography-style edits.

P2.justification: V2 adds the two-panel causal schematic in Figure 5 and relocates and renumbers the conditional-FRL plots as Figures 6–8. Table 1 also moves. Conference formatting changes headers, typography, and spacing, while existing plot designs and table structure remain substantially intact.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's worked-example appendix, v2's expanded Appendix A.2 better explains the causal setup, qualifies counterfactual-fairness connections, and distinguishes subgroup disparities from train/test shifts. These additions improve interpretation and research context. The main proofs, experimental evidence, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
